clue.text: For this expect varied forms of sagacity

indicators.note: forms of asks for the letters of the words before it set out in another shape

explanation.surface: A promise that wisdom will come to you in many different guises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varied' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder: EXPECT VARIED, reshaped by 'forms of', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel from a specialist is a practical kind of wisdom, so it stands loosely for shrewd judgement.

clue.text: Increase opportunity, getting 2 points for 100

indicators.note: getting one thing for another means a swap, the second thing giving way to the first
getting one thing for another means a swap, the second thing giving way to the first

parts.note: an opportunity is a chance
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
two compass points, east and north, give E and N

explanation.surface: Advice on boosting your prospects by trading a hundred for two points.
explanation.definitionFit: To heighten or improve something is to make it greater, a close synonym of increase.

clue.text: Safe journalist became dissipated

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter who was once careful lost his way.
explanation.walkthrough: A PETER is criminal slang for a safe, as in 'peterman', a safebreaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that petered out dwindled away to nothing, gradually fading as if scattered.

clue.text: Outcast backing fast, which is off-putting

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for outcast is read backwards

parts.note: a leper is a figurative outcast, someone shunned
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A pariah supporting a period of abstinence, which others find unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A repulsive or repelling thing is one that drives people away, putting them off.

clue.text: Article set up bets

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece is typeset, all about gambling.
explanation.definitionFit: Antes are the stakes each poker player puts in before the deal, a kind of wager.

clue.text: Rogue does his dirty work in vain

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other word

parts.note: taken as written
ill means harm or evil, the stuff of dirty work

explanation.surface: A scoundrel's wicked schemes come to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does his dirty work' paints the rogue at work; only 'dirty work' gives letters, and 'does his' is surface glue.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain is a scoundrel or wrongdoer, the same idea as a rogue.

clue.text: Song by one — one in drink

indicators.note: in places the second one inside the song word

parts.note: a chant is a simple song
I is the Roman numeral for one
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tune sung solo, while someone is tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red wine from Tuscany, so it is a kind of drink.

clue.text: With noisy entertainment old city getting older is off-putting

parts.note: a disco is a loud night of dancing
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city
ageing, spelt aging, is getting older

explanation.surface: A loud party in an ancient town where everyone is ageing makes for a dispiriting scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Ur, the ancient Sumerian city, is the crossword's favourite 'old city'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something discouraging deters or disheartens, which is what off-putting means.

clue.text: Complaint voiced by overexercise to ancient physician

parts.note: a spoken complaint after hard exercise would be 'I'm hot'
read as over plus exercise: physical education, PE, turned over

explanation.surface: Someone moaning about the heat after a workout goes to see an old doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overexercise' is one printed word doing a reversal by itself: 'over' turns the school exercise abbreviation round.
explanation.definitionFit: Imhotep was an Egyptian sage of about 2600 BC later revered as a founder of medicine.

clue.text: High-rise accommodation on the Baltic

parts.note: a high-rise building is tall
an inn offers lodging

explanation.surface: Tower-block housing by the northern sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Tallinn, capital of Estonia, is a port city lying on the Baltic coast.

clue.text: Old King Cole's bursary?

parts.note: a children's verse about a merry old monarch, plus a word that chimes with the place children sleep

explanation.surface: A grant awarded to a legendary merry monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bursary' is a rhyme for 'nursery', and the old king belongs to a children's verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint: the king is in a children's verse, and bursary chimes with a children's room.

clue.text: Line from east to west

parts.note: a London Underground line coloured red that crosses the city between its eastern and western suburbs

explanation.surface: A route drawn across the map.
explanation.walkthrough: The London Underground has a Central line running across the city from east to west.
explanation.definitionFit: London's Central line runs right across the capital from Essex in the east to the western suburbs.

clue.text: Composer made his mark

explanation.surface: A musician who became famous.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir John Stainer was a Victorian English composer of church music; read literally, the name is one who stains.
explanation.definitionFit: John Stainer wrote The Crucifixion; anyone who stains something leaves a mark on it.

clue.text: Turn over for all to see hang

parts.note: U is the British film rating for a film suitable for all audiences
to pend is to hang, as in pendant and pending

explanation.surface: Flip something over so everyone can watch it dangle.
explanation.walkthrough: A U certificate marks a British film suitable for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to turn it upside down.

clue.text: Old partner gets thinking, which can be costly

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
pensive means deep in thought

explanation.surface: A former spouse gets reflective, and that can cost a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something expensive costs a great deal, the same as costly.

clue.text: Applying pressure over Ulster is causing retribution

indicators.note: over says one piece lies spread over the other, enclosing it

parts.note: pushing is applying pressure
NI is Northern Ireland, loosely called Ulster

explanation.surface: Pressure brought to bear on Northern Ireland provoking revenge.
explanation.definitionFit: Punishing someone inflicts a penalty on them, which is retribution.

clue.text: Brainless worker — does that amount to a disaster?

indicators.note: a disaster is a wreck, so the preceding letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about whether something adds up to catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot that works mechanically without thought is a brainless worker.

clue.text: Sound quality left instrument

parts.note: timbre is the tone colour of a sound

explanation.surface: An instrument abandoned for its tone.
explanation.definitionFit: A timbrel is an old tambourine-like percussion instrument.

clue.text: Beastly creatures injure an oppressed minority

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil
gay people have long been a persecuted minority

explanation.surface: Brutes harming a persecuted group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' looks like an insult, but it just means animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Margays are small wild cats of Central and South America, so they are animals.

clue.text: Whatsit which if not thin is tacky

indicators.note: if not asks for the word without the next piece

parts.note: a thingummy is a whatsit, something whose name escapes you
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about something sticky unless it is slim.
explanation.definitionFit: Gummy means sticky, and tacky in its first sense means slightly sticky.

clue.text: Material for a celebratory meal

parts.note: a gala is a festive occasion
tea is an afternoon or evening meal

explanation.surface: Ingredients for a festive feast.
explanation.definitionFit: Galatea is a strong striped cotton fabric, so it is a material.

clue.text: Fictional hero of ragtime composer

indicators.note: a composer arranges notes, so the word before is arranged afresh

explanation.surface: The protagonist of a story by a Scott Joplin type.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Maigret is Georges Simenon's fictional Paris detective.

clue.text: Steep dip

explanation.surface: Soak or plunge.
explanation.definitionFit: To immerse is to soak something thoroughly or to plunge it briefly into liquid.

clue.text: English service that's consistently picking the winners

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, one of the armed services
ie is the abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A British body that always backs the right horses.
explanation.walkthrough: ERNIE is the machine that randomly draws winners of Britain's Premium Bonds.
explanation.definitionFit: The random number generator for British Premium Bonds is the thing that keeps selecting prize winners.

clue.text: Looking after number one is seen in unrestrained flesh

indicators.note: seen in places the word before inside the letters that follow
unrestrained means let loose, so these letters run free into a new order

explanation.surface: Egoism shows up in bodies running wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unrestrained' asks for the body word to be let loose into a new order, and 'seen in' puts the little word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting oneself first is the essence of being self-centred and egotistical.

clue.text: Shoot short feminist

clue.text: Keeping eastern leader healthy for the moment

parts.note: in trim means fit and healthy

indicators.note: a leader is the first letter of the word it goes with

explanation.surface: Holding on to the head of the east while staying fit, just for now.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim arrangement is temporary, lasting only meanwhile.

clue.text: General award given to old traveller

parts.note: Ulysses, Latin for Odysseus, wandered for ten years after Troy
a grant is a sum awarded

explanation.surface: A prize presented to an elderly wanderer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses S. Grant commanded the Union armies in the American Civil War before becoming president.
